data.description:
**Problem.** Over time, the test-writing agents tend to produce change-detector tests (snapshot/source-grep style) and grow the suite without proportionally increasing behavioral coverage. The result: slower test runs, fragile tests that lock in implementation rather than behavior, and gaps in catching bugs and review findings before code ships.

**Goal.** Calibrate test creation so that (a) change-detector-style tests are rejected at generation time rather than detected post-hoc, (b) test suite growth tracks behavioral coverage rather than line count, and (c) the suite catches a measurable share of issues currently surfaced only by code review or production bugs.

**Approach (to be brainstormed).** Builds on plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/behavioral-testing-standard.md and c13f-6196 (post-hoc detection of irrelevant test→source mappings). Likely involves: per-PR metrics on test-type composition, a pre-commit reject for change-detector patterns, prompt tuning for test-writing agents, and a feedback loop from production bugs / review findings back to test-creation prompts.

**Out of scope.** Test runner / harness changes; CI/local parity (that's cf7b-86a9); source-code bloat detectors (that's bc7f-1a0d).

Created as a North Star placeholder during /dso:prioritize-epics Phase 2; refine via /dso:brainstorm.
data.title: Test creation calibration: prevent change-detector tests and suite bloat
